answer:
Before October 2001, the LJM mail came mostly from Enron's lawyers and deal staff. A burst of mail in late September 2001 came from executives and PR. The mail_counts tool finds 55 emails mentioning LJM, LJM2, LJM1 or LJM Cayman between 1999-12-27 and 2001-09-27. Kay Mann sent the most (11), followed by Louise Kitchen and Paulo Issler (4 each). Scott Sefton, Carol Clair, James Derrick, Julia Chin and Joel Ephross sent 2 each. I read only a sample of these emails, and the sender counts exclude people who wrote from other addresses, such as Mark Palmer. Several of the 55 matches I did not read.

- **Quantitative analyst (Feb 2000):** Paulo Issler wrote the earliest LJM mail I read. On 2000-02-14 he sent Vince "LJM Pricing" files for pricing the deal with and without credit risk. On 2000-02-16 he reported that the two-factor model showed a credit loss of about 100 MM at year-end. On 2000-02-24 he wrote that Accounting argued against making any credit reserve because Enron could not liquidate the position by year-end. The same email says Accounting was in a process of unwinding the position.
- **Legal and structuring (2000):**
  - Shari Stack wrote on 2000-03-10 about an agreement under which Enron Corp. would receive all the assets of the LJM Swap Sub and pay $30 m. to LJM Equity Partners.
  - A PwC analysis forwarded by Trushar Patel assumed an LJM2 distribution based on $30m or a 25% IRR. The attachment was named Raptor v5.
  - Mary Cook's 2000-09-01 Raptor email says a notice should be addressed "Talon c/o LJM2 Co-Investment, L.P."
  - Carol Clair's 2000-08-29 email forwarded Raptor III drafts, including an "LJM Management Services Agreement."
- **Kay Mann (Jan–Feb 2001):** Her LJM mail is about turbines, not the funds themselves. On 2001-01-30 she wrote that Siemens Westinghouse had asked LJM to sign off on an agreement about Blue Girl reservation payments. On 2001-02-28 she wrote that Westinghouse had agreed LJM didn't need to sign.
- **Louise Kitchen (July 2001):** She described the AIG Highstar fund as "a new vehicle for financing similar to LJM."
- **Fastow's notice (Aug 2001):** Bridget Maronge sent a notice on 2001-08-02 saying LJM2 was "no longer a 'related party'" for proxy and financial-statement disclosure. It is signed by Andy Fastow.
- **Late September 2001:** This is the busiest month, with 10 of the 55 emails.
  - On 2001-09-21 Joel Ephross wrote about the Raptor unwind, with Raptor entities to be dissolved "the day following the LJM buyout." He added that filing had to wait until Enron had made the purchases and paid LJM for the member interests.
  - On 2001-09-25 a Wall Street Journal reporter sent questions about the board and LJM2, including the involvement of Enron officials and the general partner's compensation.
  - On 2001-09-27 Mark Palmer (PR) circulated a draft "LJM statement" to the Wall Street Journal. James Derrick forwarded it asking for thoughts.
- **False hits:** Some matches are a different Michael Miller. Chris Calger's 2001-09-26 "Mexico Person?" email lists "Mike Miller - LJM." A Michael Miller with ENW / EBS replied that Louise was looking for another Michael Miller. Kay Mann's "LM 6000" emails and Zimin Lu's "HJM" modelling email only look similar to LJM.

Counts by month from the tool show the topic running steadily from February 2000, peaking in December 2000 (8) and September 2001 (10).

I just came back from a meeting with Accounting (Ryan Siueck) and Credit (Rod

Accounting will have a meeting with AA to discuss the treatment on credit

necessary.At year-end the difference on both valuations - without and with credit risk

Accounting/Credit Group (Wes, Bill Bradford and others) yesturday, in which 
we discussed the best approach for definining credit reserves at year-end for 
the puts we own. 
2) A big chunck of the meeting was dedicated to explain AA the details of the 
deal. Little progress was made on achieving the meeting's goal.

line of action was implied on a pre-meeting we had early that morning. From 
my understanding, Accounting argues that we should not make any credit 
reserve because we could not liquidate our position by year-end.

MC-simulation for calculating the position with credit risk. The approach is 
actually a more simplified version of the model we have. I and nobody 
mentioned the results we got from our 2-factor model.
5) At that same afternoon I knew from Accounting that we are in a process of 
unwinding our position.
